name: Bechler River Trail
notes: Classic southwest Yellowstone one-way through Bechler Meadows and Bechler Canyon. The park lists multiple fords and river hazards; 9B2/9B6/9B8 are the app's named corridor camps. Published trip reports commonly put the core trail around 30–35 miles; verify seasonal ford conditions.

name: Heart Lake / Snake River Loop
notes: South Yellowstone loop around Heart Lake and the Snake/Heart confluence. The route is often reported as roughly 30–35 miles depending on the lake-side spur and campsite choice; this corridor includes every mapped backcountry camp on the loop.

name: Slough Creek Trail
notes: One-way Lamar Valley corridor from Slough Creek trailhead to the upper meadow/boundary. The three backpacker camps are kept in order; stock-only alternatives are omitted.

name: Lamar River Trail
notes: Open Lamar Valley out-and-back. The route includes every regular backpacker camp listed along the lower/middle Lamar corridor; the return to the trailhead is intentional because this is the common vehicle-friendly version.

name: Specimen Ridge to Fawn Pass Traverse
notes: Northern Yellowstone high-country traverse linking Specimen Ridge and Specimen Creek to Fawn Pass. This is a route-finding-sensitive corridor; campsite order follows the mapped trail network and should be checked against current closures.
